title: Need 5-10 people to test a tool I've been working on to easily get your game out and playable to players and, obviously, it's AI friendly. Shoot me a DM and give me a little info on your game. Only looking for those serious about their games and willing to use the tools provided.
author: TalkingPixelsStudio
selftext: I'll check back after I eat like I've never eaten before. <3

comments.author: KrakatauaMAN123
comments.body: Do you pay money to test it?

replies.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
replies.body: Not the purpose of this test so might not be for you.

replies.author: KrakatauaMAN123
replies.body:
I don't see the point of this then. So you take part of the money people have to pay more so people making games can get more info and a potential player like me can get "companions" that don't seem to do anything and test builds on a separate platform?

Like what reason should I have to give valuable information and spend time on things like surveys?

replies.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
replies.body:
I meant that right now I'm trying to see what helps and doesn't help and, if It was a paid gig, I don't feel as though I would get the results I want. I get where your coming from and will be having a paid test at some point but just not atm.

  
Hope that clears some things up. Have a good one\~

replies.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
replies.body: Not doing any paid plans for awhile if ever. I added that in to be transparent though.

replies.author: -svde-
replies.body: what you’re saying it that the purpose of the test is to get labor- that is done as an actual paid job requiring time, knowledge, presence, and sometimes skills- for free. this is not a great way to approach thigns in general but this response really compounds the problem

replies.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
replies.body: The purpose is to find bugs, gather feedback and see what more we could do to promote devs games. Maybe we’re not going to see the to eye but some folks, including myself, enjoy play testing and trying out new tools. Look forward to trying out whatever you’ve been cooking and good luck to you as well.

replies.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
replies.body: Oof look at that I even beat spellcheck lol. Sleep time soon…maybe

replies.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
replies.body: Oh, an example of some feedback I got from the last test for the final tool for the platform that's been in the oven, is how a lot of games don't offer controller options for those that have certain conditions or would just like the option to edit the controller and play the way it's comfortable for them. I was going to push this last build public before reaching out to the tester and chatting for awhile. I instantly started doing my best to implement changes to controller layout based on the things they said. Might not be perfect right away but some things you don't always think about could end up being a players favorite feature.

replies.author: TalkingPixelsStudio
replies.body:
**Talking Pixels** (talkingpixels.games) — what's there and why it helps:

* **Store + creator page** — sell games and assets with versioned files and licence keys; your page is yours, placement is never bought.
* **Devlog on the store page** — followers see progress where they'd buy, no separate blog to maintain.
* **Playtests and demos** — open or closed testing with sign-ups, tester-only builds, and a short survey after each session that lands in your dashboard, so you learn what's working instead of guessing.
* **Bug reports with a loop** — reports are tied to the build and marked when fixed; confirmed reports reward the tester.
* **Looking for Group + presence** — see who's online and in what; group posts per game with honest tags, so small multiplayer games actually find players.
* **Game hubs** — reviews, discussion boards and your announcements in one place per game.
* **Chat that files itself** — meet someone in a game and the conversation lands under that game; blocking and reporting built in.
* **Creators inbox** — player messages arrive sorted by intent (bug, question, praise, request) with context like "12 hours in", so the important ones surface first.
* **Mods with your approval** — you decide if your game takes mods; approved ones list on the page with the author credited.
* **Team Finder and groups** — studios looking for people and people looking for studios, with listings that expire so the board stays alive.
* **Spark (community backing)** — supporters fund a project in progress; money moves backer-to-creator, the platform never holds it.
* **Levels and Pixels** — hours, tested games, finished playtests and confirmed reports earn levels and the platform currency; Pixels can't be bought.
* **Companions** — creatures found by playing, with a Portal you throw Pixels into; no loot boxes, no odds, no trading market.
* **Credits that stick** — every artist and tester is named in a registry that follows the game, with a People page.
* **Shop and monthly magazine** — cosmetic only, anything bought with money is earnable too; each issue hides a code.
* **Creator dashboard** — wishlists, plays, playtest data and a payout ledger that shows every sale, fee and transfer.
* **Fees in plain numbers** — 10% + processing at cost, shown before you set a price; free games are free to list.
* **Any engine** — guides for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker, Construct, Ren'Py, Twine, LÖVE and Bevy.

Closed alpha now; sign-up form on the site.
